headline: The 3090 trained its own model and mailed it home
lede: Stage 2 of the Plaicraft research pipeline is merged in retrogames-rl: the trainer left the game repo, the dataset rode rsync to the 3090 box, and the box pushed its own trained model back under its deploy key. It scores better than v2 — and the numbers now come with the honesty kit attached.

notes.text: v3 (trained on the 3090, scored once on Studio): pad 0.9124 | move 0.9752 | loss 0.1266 | intent rare-class F1 0.7373 — beats v2 on four measures; intent accuracy −0.0008 sits below the one-feature-copy ceiling that v2's 0.986 exactly equalled.

score.mjs now prints precision/recall/F1 for the rare swing class next to accuracy, plus the always-0 (0.976) and single-feature (0.986) baselines — accuracy claims can no longer hide that a=1 lives in only 2.37% of rows.

Determinism got tested instead of claimed: seed 7 on the box (x86_64) vs the Studio (arm64) is byte-identical, 0 of 1493 weights. The shipped v2 is NOT reproducible — its training corpus was never hashed — so every artifact now carries its corpus sha and runtime in its meta.
A retrogames PR removed the last training code from the game repo (trainer + npm alias) — merged the same shift once #601 released; the arcade ships data and scores, the 3090 trains.
